question: Which skin layer is destroyed in a full-thickness burn?
explanation: Full-thickness burns destroy the entire epidermis and dermis, frequently extending into subcutaneous fat, muscle, or bone. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why might a severe third-degree burn present with reduced pain at the center of the wound?

options.B: The skin lacks pain receptors in deep layers
options.C: Sensory nerve endings have been destroyed

explanation: Because full-thickness burns destroy nerve endings within the dermal layer, the center of the burn is often insensate to touch and pain. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary domestic location where burn injuries most frequently occur?
explanation: Cooking appliances, hot liquids, and open flames make the kitchen the most common site for domestic burns. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h2)

question: A family uses a low-level kerosene stove placed directly on the kitchen floor. What is the major mechanical risk this setup presents?

options.B: Easy tipping by crawling or walking children
options.D: Rapid accumulation of toxic carbon monoxide

explanation: Floor-level stoves are easily knocked over by moving children, resulting in massive scalds or ignition of clothing. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the safest direction to position pot handles on a cooking stove?

options.A: Inward toward the back of the stove
options.B: Dangling downward below the stove base
options.D: Parallel to the front edge of the counter

explanation: Turning handles inward prevents children from grabbing them and pulling hot contents onto themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which practice is most effective in preventing hot bathwater scalds in toddlers?

options.A: Testing the water temperature with an elbow or thermometer
options.B: Adding cold water only after the child enters the tub
options.C: Turning off the water heater completely during bath time
options.D: Relying on the child to verbalize if the water feels too warm

explanation: Adult hands have tougher skin and may misjudge water that is dangerously hot for a child's sensitive skin. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why is the internal damage from an electrical burn often deceptive?

options.A: Skin heals faster than underlying muscle
options.B: Electrical current only affects the outer layer of the epidermis
options.C: Current bypasses the torso entirely and affects only limbs
options.D: Electricity travels along blood vessels and nerves causing deep injury

explanation: Electricity follows internal paths of least resistance, meaning severe deep tissue damage can occur beneath relatively small skin entry and exit wounds. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which type of chemical agent generally causes deeper tissue destruction through liquefactive necrosis?
explanation: Alkalis penetrate tissues more deeply than acids by dissolving proteins and fats, resulting in severe liquefactive necrosis. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h4)

question: How often should household smoke alarm batteries ideally be tested?

options.D: Only when moving into a new home

explanation: Monthly testing ensures the alarm system is operational and the battery charge remains strong. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a pre-arranged outdoor meeting place during a home fire escape plan?

options.A: To store emergency first aid kits and water supplies
options.B: To wait for law enforcement officers to secure the perimeter
options.C: To quickly account for all household members and prevent re-entry
options.D: To provide a staging area for fighting the active fire

explanation: A designated meeting place ensures everyone has escaped safely and prevents anyone from running back into a burning building. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why does a child sustain a deeper burn than an adult when exposed to the same hot liquid for an identical duration?

options.A: Children produce less natural body oil
options.D: Children have a higher metabolic rate

explanation: Pediatric skin is significantly thinner than adult skin, meaning heat penetrates faster and causes deeper tissue damage in less time. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which factor primarily increases burn vulnerability in elderly populations?

options.B: Higher threshold for thermal pain perception
options.D: Decreased tactile sensitivity and slower mobility

explanation: Reduced sensation prevents older adults from feeling extreme heat quickly, and slowed mobility hinders their ability to escape hazards. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h6)

question: What is the recommended fluid and temperature for cooling a fresh thermal burn?

options.A: Cool running tap water for 10 to 20 minutes
options.B: Warm soapy water to disinfect the area

explanation: Cool running tap water safely removes heat from the tissue without causing vasoconstriction or further cellular damage associated with ice. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why is the application of ice or iced water contraindicated in fresh burn management?

options.C: It permanently stains the epidermal tissue black
options.D: It causes severe vasoconstriction and deepens tissue injury

explanation: Extreme cold causes blood vessels to constrict sharply, reducing blood flow and converting a partial-thickness burn into a deeper injury. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a community health nurse regarding burn prevention during home visits?

options.B: Installing electrical wiring and smoke alarms personally
options.C: Identifying environmental hazards and educating the family

explanation: Nurses assess domestic environments to spot potential risks and provide practical, culturally appropriate education to prevent injuries. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h8)

question: Why must nurse-led community burn education be culturally sensitive and tailored to local resources?

options.A: Traditional remedies are scientifically proven to be superior to cold water
options.B: Families are unlikely to adopt recommendations that ignore their economic and lifestyle realities
options.C: Standard international guidelines are illegal in developing regions
options.D: Cultural practices completely eliminate the risk of thermal injuries

explanation: Education is only effective when it respects local context and offers realistic alternatives that families can actually implement within their homes. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h8)
